text: Caitlín is an Irish form of the French name Catherine. It stands as one spelling among many. Countless historical figures have carried the name since the twelfth century. The best-known folkloric bearer is Caitlín Ní hUallacháin. That family name survives in many spellings across Kilkenny and neighbouring Clare. People also read Caitlin as a fresh picture of Ireland. W. B. Yeats shaped this image of the nation. His play Cathleen ni Houlihan first reached the stage in 1902. Later writers sometimes spell the name Kathleen O'Hoolihan. In some texts Caitlin becomes the wife of the one-eyed giant Balor.
